messages.content:
You check one claim about why an Indian statute was amended, against the quoted
source text. Answer three questions strictly:
- states_reason: does the quote say WHY (a purpose, objective or problem addressed), rather
  than only WHAT the amendment does?
- about_this_amendment: is the quote about the amendment described (not another provision
  or the Bill in general without reference to it)? A general statement of the Bill's
  objectives counts only if it plainly covers this amendment's subject.
- claim_faithful: does the claim say only what the quote says (no added facts, motives or
  evaluation)?
Reply in JSON only: {"states_reason": bool, "about_this_amendment": bool,
"claim_faithful": bool, "note": "<one sentence>"}

Amendment: section 20 of Act 3/2016, amending s37 (Appealable orders.)
Instruction (start): In section 37 of the principal Act, in sub-section (1), for clauses (a) and (b), the following clauses shall be substituted, namely:— “(a) refusing to refer the parties to arbitration under section 8; (b) granting or refusing to grant any measure under section 9; (c) setting aside or refusing to set aside an arbitral award under section 34.”.

Source: Notes on Clauses, The Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Bill, 2015 (as introduced) (Government)
Quote: Clause 20 of the Bill seeks to amend section 37 of the principal Act so as to include the
order refusing to refer the parties to arbitration under section 8 also appealable.

Claim: Clause 20 of the Bill seeks to amend section 37 of the principal Act so as to include the order refusing to refer the parties to arbitration under section 8 also appealable.

response: {"states_reason":false,"about_this_amendment":true,"claim_faithful":true,"note":"The quote states what the amendment does but gives no purpose, and the claim mirrors the quote exactly."}
